verdict_summary: The IR geometry holds: shell budget and co-orbital kernel reproduced exactly (3.66/1.91/1.75 W/m2 per 1 %, kernel 0.284, 1.428 W/m2 per 1 %), and far-side placement is the best IR geometry. The headline limits do not hold. They rest on an unachievable eps_f 0.05 front at no PV cost, a superseded parameter set (22 % ceiling), a tau <= 0.9 cloud with no collision or shading cost, and a 2.5x thermostat credit that the study's own polar residuals cap near 2x. Revised central: 0.4-0.5 % / 3.7-4.9 % / 9.6 % at 0.1/1/4 W/m2 (1.0-1.4e38 / 1.0-1.3e39 / 2.5e39 FLOP/s), vs 1.6 / 13.8 / 18.7 %. The sky binds first (0.44-1.0 %). The far-side cloud also creates an Earth-debris hazard the shell does not have.

errors.claim: Ceiling 22 % / 1.1e40 FLOP/s; 1 W/m2 allows 13.8 % (50 % of ceiling); 4 W/m2 is fleet-limited at 18.7 %
errors.problem: All mass/compute numbers use the superseded research5 "2100 mid" set (eta0 0.25, -0.26 %/K, eps 0.86/0.93, packing 0.93, film 0.165 kg/m2), not the repo's current v4 mid (0.215, -0.34 %/K, 0.85/0.90, 0.92, 0.195 kg/m2, podFrac 0.06). Coverage of a mass-limited fleet does not depend on PV efficiency, so the r^2 and areal-density changes dominate.
errors.correct_value: repo ceiling f 0.142 (0.899 AU), 5.78e39 FLOP/s, B_ss 7.96e21 kg; fleet-limited at 1 AU 0.121 (no shading), 0.094-0.097 with overlap shading

errors.claim: Low-e front eps_f 0.05-0.10 ("transparent-conductive low-e coating") over the PV, at no PV cost
errors.problem: No PV-compatible front reaches 0.05. TMM/Drude: ITO 5 ohm/sq eps_h 0.108 (PV x0.86, alpha +0.06); IO:H 5 ohm/sq 0.103 (PV x0.93) but indium is short x3e4-5e4 of a BSE-bounded Mercury inventory; AZO floor 0.14-0.16 (PV x0.81-0.89, Zn short x9); FTO/ATO/TNO floor 0.19-0.32 at PV x0.5-0.85 (Sn short x1e4, Nb x70); Ag DMD 0.10 at PV x0.76 (Ag short x5e3); Al DMD transmits 0.2-0.5; FeCl3-graphene needs 40 layers for 0.10 (PV x0.69: its 2-D Drude weight is too small, omega*tau >> 1 in the IR). Mercury-native Al/Mg nanomesh must have pitch >= 0.6 um (holes below waveguide cutoff block 1.1 um light): eps_h 0.11-0.15 at PV x0.72-0.79.
errors.correct_value: plan with eps_h ~0.15 (0.13 toward Earth), PV x0.79, alpha 0.81, 1 % NIR leakage: gross IR 0.40 W/m2 per 1 % (f 1 %) to 0.45 (f 14 %), not 0.15

errors.problem: Uses eps_b 0.93. Design/repo eps_b 0.90 gives 375-380 K (Tj 111-116 C) for eps_f 0.10-0.05; the design spec's own computed floor for a 15 um enamel (0.73) gives 393-399 K (Tj 129-135 C, energy/op x1.28-1.32). With 85-95 % of the heat now leaving the back, eps_b is first-order and unmeasured.

errors.claim: Energy/op x1.12-1.15, -16-19 % FLOP/J, +35-46 % mass per W
errors.problem: Repo params with the study's ideal front: -19/-23 % FLOP/J, +40/+43 % g/W. Real fronts (PV loss + alpha): -27 to -43 % FLOP/J, +52 to +91 % g/W; with eps_b 0.73 down to -52 % / +105 %. The required front NIR mirror (40-60 TiO2/SiO2 layers, 5-8 um, +12-20 g/m2, -3-5 % PV) is not costed.
errors.correct_value: central Mercury-native: FLOP/J 6.98e13 (-34 % vs shell 1.06e14), 1.54 g/W (+72 %)

errors.claim: Cancelling up to 2.5 X of gross IR with an L1 shade is hydrologically equivalent to an uncancelled X
errors.problem: Single metric with an inconsistent yardstick: the uncancelled case ignores the swarm IR's own fast precipitation response (92 % absorbed in the atmosphere); a CO2-like X (dP +1.6 X %) gives 2.1 X even by that metric. The study's own residuals (June 70-90N +0.41, annual 60-90 +0.23 W/m2 per W/m2 cancelled) exceed a CO2-like X at G = 1.9 X (full cancellation) / 2.0 X (optimal partial shade); over coefficient uncertainty the multi-metric allowance is 1.4-1.8 X median, 0.8-1.2 X at the 10th percentile. Passive swarm IR is also worse than CO2 per W/m2 at the summer pole (G <= 0.57 X by the same metrics).
errors.correct_value: k <= 2.0 nominal, 1.5 for planning, shade sized by optimisation (partial offset), pending a GCM ensemble

errors.claim: Geometric cap 0.9 x 23.3 % = 21 %; coverage up to 13.8-18.7 % in the L3 +-84/|lat|<=30 patch
errors.problem: All co-orbital sails share a = 0.9987 AU, so radial separation exists only through eccentricity. A random-phase cloud has 3-56 collisions per sail per year (dv_r 0.3-0.8 km/s, dv_t ~9 km/s; tau 0.3-0.9, e_max 0.005-0.05). Collision-free requires node-stacked lattices with metre-level radial clearance passing at up to 15 km/s. Overlap shading wastes 25-34 % (random) or 20-31 % (stacked) of sail area at tau 0.6-0.9: intercepted share at tau_sum 0.9 is 13.8 %, not 21 %. Derelicts collide 9-19 times per year in the cloud (0.6-2.8 in the shell).
errors.correct_value: plan tau_sum <= 0.4-0.6 (f <= 7.6-10.5 % in this patch) with a 1.2-1.3x mass penalty; derelict capture < ~3 weeks

errors.claim: Uncontrolled sails never come within 0.29 AU of Earth
errors.problem: Holds only for sails that stay sun-pointed with no control; real uncontrolled sails tumble (beta 0.002: 0.21 AU) and break up. Each sail carries ~69 low-beta parts (250 kg hub, 4 x 109 kg booms, 64 x 5 kg terminals) that pass within 0.035 AU dozens of times in 3 kyr; Myr horseshoe-to-Earth-crossing transitions are not integrated. Interior-shell derelicts never reach Earth.
errors.correct_value: uncontrolled loss probability <= 1e-14-1e-12 per sail (f 1-14 %) to keep dense-part impacts < 10 % of the natural >= 10 kg flux, or every separable part with beta >= 0.002

errors.claim: Fine dust < 1e-7-3e-6 of the 3e19 kg/yr loss stream; the swarm is a net dust sink
errors.problem: Computed for release at 0.91 AU. At 1 AU (the recommended placement) the study's own per-grain Earth-hit probability is 4e-5-2e-2 without re-sweeping; only re-sweeping by the cloud keeps it near 1e-7-1e-6. Meteoroid ejecta are released in Earth's orbit.
errors.correct_value: allowed fine-dust fraction 6e-12 (no re-sweep) to 2e-6 (re-swept); meteoroid ejecta 1e-4-0.2x natural influx (re-swept), up to 5e3x (not)

errors.claim: Sky: 0.31 lux per 1 % at rho_v 0.003; full-moon cap 0.8 %, 2.4 % with rho_v 0.001
errors.problem: Geometry re-verified (0.33 lux per 1 %), but the design-spec reflectance toward Earth is film ~0.00035 + hinge strips 0.0008 + scribes 0.0006 + hems 0.0004 = 0.0021 before vanes; matte white vanes (the study's fix) add 0.0035; specular vanes average about the same when their glints sweep Earth; only black vanes keep ~0.0024. rho 0.001 is below the hardware floor.
errors.correct_value: full-moon cap 0.44 % (matte vanes) to 1.0-1.15 % (black or specular vanes)

errors.claim: L3 +-6 deg keep-out stops specular NIR glints (beam half-angle 2.9 deg)
errors.problem: Design spec edge zones (22 % of area) tilt up to 3.7 deg at a 3 K residual, so the NIR retro-beam spans 7.4 deg: sails at psi 165-174 glint at Earth, +0.67 W/m2 per 1 % (4x the claimed b5 IR). Running the film 27 K above its 348 K stress-free temperature curls free edges ~33 deg (0.122 /m/K x dT x 0.176 m).
errors.correct_value: keep-out +-15 deg (kernel +1 %) and laminate stress-free at the hot operating temperature

errors.claim: Faces emit Lambertian with the hemispherical emissivity
errors.problem: Glass emits more toward Earth (0-45 deg: 0.87) than hemispherically (0.82); low-e conductors emit ~15 % less.
errors.correct_value: design glass front 1.48 W/m2 per 1 % (not 1.43); low-e toward-Earth eps ~0.85x hemispherical

errors.claim: At the 22 % ceiling the interior shell reaches 279-283 W/m2, at the runaway limit
errors.problem: Physics verified (3.66 IR + 0.49 NIR - 2.38 dimming per 1 %; 47.8 % far-side fronts at 1 %, 42.7 % at 22 %), but the ceiling is superseded.
errors.correct_value: at the repo ceiling (14.2 %, 0.899 AU): +25.7 W/m2, 264 W/m2 absorbed, 6.5 CO2 doublings (repo earthImpact: +30, 268)

errors.problem: Closed-loop test is CR3BP, circular Earth orbit, i = 0 only. Plausible (Venus passes ~3e-3 m/s each, Jupiter tide ~1e-7 m/s2 periodic, authority 2.4e-5 m/s2) but untested. The binding control problem is the metre-level collision lattice and derelict capture.

errors.claim: Sub-bandgap light reflected to Earth is absorbed at 0.70
errors.problem: 1.1-2.5 um planetary absorptance is ~0.75-0.80 (water-vapour bands, lower NIR cloud albedo).

too_optimistic: eps_f 0.05 with no PV, absorptance or filter penalty: the headline 13.8 % at 1 W/m2 rests on it; realistic Mercury-native fronts give 2.5-3x the gross IR per coverage and -34 % FLOP/J.
Superseded research5 parameters: ceiling 22 % / 1.1e40 instead of the repo's 14.2 % / 5.8e39; fleet-limited 18.7 % instead of 9.6 %.
tau up to 0.9 in a co-orbital patch with no collision, choreography or shading cost.
Thermostat credit 2.5 X: the study's own polar-summer residuals cap it near 2 X (median 1.4-1.8 X under uncertainty).
Passive limits treat swarm IR like CO2 per W/m2; its near-Sun origin puts 1.4x the global mean on the summer pole (vs ~0.8x for CO2), so passive G <= ~0.6 X by the polar metric.
"Uncontrolled sails never within 0.29 AU": uncontrolled sails tumble (0.21 AU) and dense parts reach 0.035 AU; Myr fate not integrated.
Dust and ejecta budgets computed for 0.91 AU release, not for the recommended 1 AU placement.
rho_v 0.001 and "matte vanes" for the sky: matte white vanes brighten the cloud; 0.001 is below the hinge-strip and scribe floor.
eps_b 0.93 assumed for a back that now carries 85-95 % of the heat; the design spec's computed floor is 0.73.

Retro-reflected NIR and the low-e layer are not reconciled: the conductor must be outermost (a 5-8 um dielectric NIR mirror above it restores eps ~0.6-0.8), and the conductor absorbs 1-12 % of the 1.1-2.5 um band on the way in and out.
too_conservative: Latitude band |lat| <= 30 deg: lon 75-174 x |lat| <= 60 has 2.04x the solid angle for only +6 % IR per coverage (kernel 0.303 vs 0.284); the whole far hemisphere costs +3 % for 2.1x. Using it halves tau, halving collision rates and shading losses.

All absorbed IR counted as forcing with efficacy 1: 92 % is absorbed in the atmosphere, much of it near the emission level, so the ERF may be 0.6-0.9 of the absorbed flux (temperature limits looser by 10-60 %; the precipitation penalty is larger).

Directional front (b3) set aside as a technology bet: against realistic low-e penalties, b3 (85 C chips, no PV loss, 0.34 W/m2 per 1 %) gives ~1.75x more FLOP/s per W/m2 of IR than a Mercury-native low-e front and should get equal R&D priority.

Uniform L1 shade: shifting the shade cloud toward the summer pole (penumbral spot radius 1.16 R_E) can cut the polar-summer residual that binds k ~2; with T and P alone an optimised partial shade allows 4.2 X.
missing: Sail-sail collision rates and a derelict-cascade criterion (computed here: random cloud 3-56 per sail-year; derelicts 9-19 per year in the cloud, 0.6-2.8 in the shell).
A dense-part rule: every separable part needs beta >= 0.002 (or a tether), else loss probability <= 1e-14-1e-12 per sail.

Earth links: the 60 patch terminals are on the back and never see Earth (always 3-45 deg from the Sun in the sunward hemisphere); only the 4 corner terminals see past the edge. 10 cm apertures give 20-80 bit/s at 1.41 AU, so Earth traffic needs dedicated 10-30 m relays at psi <= 120 deg (>= 30 deg elongation). Lines to psi >= 165 pass 11-56 R_sun from the Sun. One-way latency is 11.8-16.6 min, and capacity per aperture pair is ~250x lower than from the shell's 0.09 AU near cap.

Pod beta mismatch: pods have beta ~0.0017 (4 t, 4431 m2 of wings per MW), so co-orbital a = 0.99943 AU, 1.1e8 m outside the sail layer: out of Starlink-class range and in the sails' shadow. Fix with ~6000 m2 of thin absorbing film per MW pod (~30-60 kg) to match beta 0.004.

Front NIR-mirror specification: <= 1 % leakage (each 1 % of sunlight returned diffusely adds 0.027 W/m2 per 1 %; the design spec's textured cell returns 20 % diffusely = +0.54), mass, PV loss, ordering under the conductor.
Stress-free lamination temperature for a 375-400 K film (edge curl ~33 deg otherwise).
An explicit sky policy: full moon (0.44-1.0 %), quarter moon (0.04-0.1 %), or 10x zodiacal light (2-5e-5). The sky binds at or below the 0.1 W/m2 climate limit.
Secular differential precession of the lattice (planetary node and e-vector drift) needs continuous metre-level relative navigation for every sail.
Thermostat failure mode: with G up to 2 X cancelled, losing the shade must trigger swarm feathering within months; this needs a control channel independent of the shade.
A GCM ensemble (GeoMIP-G1-like) with a 330-400 K diluted source within 45 deg of the Sun plus an L1 shade, before any thermostat credit is taken.

revised_limits.basis: Repo model v4 mid (src/model copied unchanged to skeptic/model): ceiling f = 0.142, 5.78e+39 FLOP/s, steady fleet 7.96e+21 kg. Central front = Mercury-native Al mesh (0.6 um pitch, 48 nm lines): eps_h 0.146, 0.128 toward Earth, PV x0.79, alpha +0.01, 1 % diffuse NIR leakage; eps_b 0.90; IR 0.396 W/m2 per 1 %; FLOP/J 6.98e+13 (shell 1.06e14). Thermostat credit k = gross/X: 1.5 (robust, planning) and 2.0 (nominal multi-metric); passive k = 1. Fleet mass includes random-overlap shading in the 23 % patch.

repo_unconstrained_ceiling.note: the study used the superseded research5 ceiling 0.2217 / 1.115e40

sky_limit.criterion: post-twilight ground illuminance <= full moon (0.25 lux) at an 18 deg solar depression, ecliptic vertical (study rule; geometry re-verified: 0.33 vs 0.31 lux per 1 % at rho 0.003)
sky_limit.note: rho_v 0.001 (the study's 2.4 %) is below the hardware floor of 0.0021 (hinge strips, scribe lines, hems) unless those are blackened too.

revised_limits.binding_order_central: sky full-moon 0.44-1.0 % ~ climate 0.1 W/m2 0.38-0.51 % << climate 1 W/m2 3.7-4.9 % < fleet mass + shading 9.6 %. At the 1 W/m2 limit the post-twilight glow is ~1-3 lux (civil-twilight level) for 1-2 h every night.

revised_recommendation: Keep the far-side co-orbital cloud as the IR-preferred geometry, but restate it. (1) Make the sky the headline Earth constraint and choose a sky policy first: with design-spec hardware the post-twilight glow reaches full-moon level at 0.44-1.0 % coverage (1.2-2.7e38 FLOP/s), about the same as the 0.1 W/m2 climate limit. (2) For a climate cap, plan with a Mercury-native low-e front (Al/Mg mesh, pitch >= 0.6 um, eps_h ~0.15, PV x0.79, Tj ~106-112 C), a measured eps_b >= 0.85, and an optimised partial L1 shade with k <= 1.5-2. That gives 1 W/m2 -> 3.7-4.9 % (1.0-1.3e39 FLOP/s, 17-22 % of the repo's 5.8e39 ceiling, ~2200-2250); 0.1 W/m2 -> 0.4-0.5 %; 4 W/m2 -> ~9.6 %, limited by mass plus shading. (3) Prerequisites before it becomes the headline: a collision-free node-stacked orbit lattice with metre-level relative navigation and < 3-week derelict capture; beta >= 0.002 for every separable part; stress-free lamination at the hot temperature; NIR keep-out +-15 deg and a front NIR mirror with <= 1 % leakage; relay craft for Earth links; a GeoMIP-style GCM ensemble for the thermostat. (4) Widen the cloud to |lat| <= 60 deg (2x room, +6 % IR) and fund directional-emitter fronts (b3), which avoid the hot-chip and PV penalties and give ~1.75x more compute per W/m2. (5) Keep the 0.85-0.92 AU shell as the fallback: debris-safe for Earth, but passive-limited to 0.065 % / 0.65 % / 2.5 % at 0.1/1/4 W/m2.
model_changes: Use the repo's own v4 mid parameters everywhere (ceiling 14.2 %, 5.78e39 FLOP/s); drop the research5 22 %/1.1e40 numbers from the Earth-safe tables.

Split intercepted light into alpha (IR, 0.95) and 1-alpha (NIR, 0.75-0.80); the repo currently sends all f S0 to IR.
Low-e front parameters: pvEta0 x (0.72-0.86), alpha +0.01-0.06, eps_toward_Earth = 0.85 eps_h for conductors; expose eps_b with range 0.73-0.90 (it now sets Tj).
Co-orbital cloud: patch fraction (0.233 for |lat| <= 30; 0.476 for |lat| <= 60, lon 75-174), tau_sum = -ln(1 - f/patch), mass penalty 1/[(1-e^-tau)/tau], and a planning cap tau_sum <= 0.6.

Thermostat: gross cap k X with k = 1.5 (default) to 2.0; size the shade by optimisation (output dT, dP incl. -1.18 % per W/m2 of swarm IR fast response, polar annual and June residuals), not by full cancellation.

Sky: luminance 1730 x rho_eff cd/m2 per 1 % in the patch, ground light 0.33 x rho_eff/0.003 lux per 1 % at 18 deg depression; rho_eff default 0.0024 (black vanes), 0.0056 (matte vanes); a selectable sky criterion, shown as the first binding limit.
Debris: co-orbital-specific outputs (dense-part loss probability limit, derelict collision rate 9-19 /yr x tau/0.6, re-swept dust p_hit 1e-7-1e-6).
Earth flag text: shell at the repo ceiling +26-30 W/m2 (264-268 absorbed, ~6.5 doublings), not "at the runaway limit".
render_notes: From Earth at night: two luminous wings along the ecliptic flanking the Sun, like an exaggerated zodiacal light, from ~3-15 deg to 45 deg elongation and +-15-20 deg in ecliptic latitude. Brightest within 10 deg of the Sun. Luminance ~1730 x rho cd/m2 per 1 % (4-10 cd/m2 per 1 %; 16-50 cd/m2 near the Sun at a 4-5 % cloud). That is ~1e3-1e4x the zodiacal light (~1.7e-3 cd/m2 at 30 deg).

After dusk in the west and before dawn in the east: a tilted cone along the ecliptic, as bright as civil twilight once coverage exceeds ~3 %; 0.25-0.6 lux per 1 % at an 18 deg solar depression; gone once the Sun is > 45 deg down. At latitudes >= ~45 deg in summer it never sets: low in the north at midnight, 0.001-0.035 lux per 1 % at 50-60 N.
Colour: near-white with a faint violet-blue cast. The integrated glow is dominated by hardware (vanes, hinge strips, scribes, hems), not the navy film.
Daytime: invisible except in the solar aureole; during total eclipses, two bright wings out to 45 deg along the ecliptic, with a dark gap within 3-15 deg of the Sun (keep-out).
Telescopically: granular glitter of 9-16 mag glints (vanes, film edge zones); near L3 (elongation < 7.5 deg) a specular retro-reflection surge visible only in coronagraphs and eclipses.
No shadows, transits or flicker on Earth. The L1 thermostat (1-2 R_E across, 1.57e6 km sunward) is invisible to the eye: a faint haze on the solar disk in a filtered solar telescope.
Thermal IR: the wings glow at ~1.5 W/m2/sr per 1 % with low-e fronts (7.5 with glass fronts), invisible to the eye.

System view: two crescent arcs on Earth's orbit centred ~130 deg ahead of and behind Earth, each ~75-84 deg long (90-165/174 deg from Earth), +-0.5 AU tall (|lat| <= 30; +-0.87 AU if extended to 60). Gap around L3; nothing inside Earth's orbit except the tiny L1 cloud. Co-rotates with Earth: stationary in Earth's frame, one turn per year against the stars.

Close-up: 279 m navy diamonds with a faint metallic sheen (mesh low-e, specular, seen only near the Sun-viewer line). Backs glow at 370-400 K in thermal IR; corner vanes are the brightest visible parts (black if the sky policy demands it).

Texture: not a smooth shell. Local optical depth 0.2-0.5, with sails stacked along shared node lines (overlap bands) and gaps. Each sail bobs +-i in latitude once a year and traces a small epicycle; pods carry extra absorbing film to match the sails' beta.
Default coverage to render: <= 1 % (sky limit) or ~4-5 % (1 W/m2 with k 1.5-2), not 13.8-22 %. Keep the 0.85-0.92 AU shell only as the labelled "unconstrained / unsafe" comparison.
Dynamics overlay: tumbling-derelict tadpoles to 0.21 AU of Earth, dense-part horseshoes to 0.035 AU, the L1 24-day instability.
